Even after we called someone to check it they could not fully close it as it was hanging sideways.  The window on room 411 opens to the road where bars run all night. The music was not allowing us to sleep and at 2am my wife had to go to reception to complain as the reception would not answer. After their lack of interest and the answer that they don't have a method to monitor complaints, we decided we would not get back to Best Western again.  It seems silly now to point that the bar did not have light drinks or that shampoo was present but not shower gel or that there are hardly any power points other than one free next to the bed.  If you have to come here just make sure you avoid 411 and ask for a room not on the road of you want to sleep.  There are many good hotels in Manila and there is no reason to take this.

Karl did not get tired of answering my queries be it about the course or other SCUBA matters which are not really related to the course. But what really sets them apart are the instructors who I believe are doing this more as a hobby.  They also do not confine themselves to the basic course requirements but incorporate lessons that they learned from personal experience and other courses that they teach. But your relationship with MDA does not end with certification. You are welcome to dive with them after. (I would be diving with them more often if I had the time). As a final word I am so happy with their service that I will be pursuing further training with MDA this coming year.

The elevator only works when you put your room key in it for extra security.  Please note that the entire compound of hotels and attractions is surrounded by a pretty ghetto area.  The actual city of Manilla is about 10 clicks away.  Check in was fine.  I arrived late night so didn't have any lines to deal with.  I paid through Hotels.com.  I didn't need my credit card or have to leave a cash deposit on the room but you might if you're staying for longer.  I just handed them my passport and they took care of the rest.    The hallways aren't air conditioned.  Some vending machines on each floor.  2 Queen bed room (the least expensive):  No carpets in the room.  A small flat screen.  One standard electronic room safe.  They give you 2 bottles of water, 2 bars of soap, 2 surprisingly decent toothbrushes (saved one to use on the plane), 2 mini tubes of Colgate toothpaste, 2 towels, 2 plastic cups and 2 pairs of disposable slippers.  A/C has decent power but you can only choose between on and off.  Regular toilet but no bath tub.  Just a stand up shower with a curtain. Smoking rooms are optional.  Wifi signal was weak.  Will only let you sign one device in (they give you a log in name and password).  Directly across from the entrance is a huge construction project that looks like it just began (March 2014) so if you're a light sleeper, request a room not facing the front.  McDonalds is next door (24/7) and the casino is across the small street from there.  Casino was alright.  You're allowed to smoke.  Not allowed to tip.  The general area has tables of about 100 to 300 peso minimums 5000-10000 peso maximums.  A lot of slot machines (about half the casino).  24/7.  I slept through the free breakfast.  Checked out right at noon.  Everyone else seemed to be checked out already so I skipped that line too.  Handed the girl my keycards and only had to wait 1 minute for her to say I was checked out.  Overall, okay hotel.   The actual city of Manilla is 10 clicks away so only good as a layover Hotel.  Rooms could be better.  They were adequately clean.  Skip the free bus to the airport.  Get your own air conditioned cab out front.  Should only be about 100 pesos.  550 (12.50 American) per person airport fee when leaving the country as well.  They won't make change so make sure you visit the change counter inside the terminal or have the correct change ready.  Would stay again if I had a one day layover.  Would find one in actual Manilla if I was going as a tourist.
